newsitem.title: FRANCE: France delays Dassault documents decision.
newsitem.headline: France delays Dassault documents decision.

text.p: France's new Socialist justice minister, Elisabeth Guigou, plans no quick decision over secret documents her Gaullist predecessor refused to give Belgium for a bribery case against warplane maker Serge Dassault, government officials said on Friday.

Belgian police are investigating accusations that Dassault Aviation paid 600 million Belgian francs ($17 million) to political parties to secure a contract to fit air defence systems to Belgian F-16 jets in the late 1980s. The company denies it.
Gaullist Justice Minister Jacques Toubon refused to turn over documents on the grounds they contained state secrets.
A senior official in Guigou's office told reporters Toubon's decision was being re-examined.
"Justice systems should help each other but there is also the question of national interest," the official said. "We can't make a decision about this in just a few days."
A Liege court issued an international arrest warrant in May last year for Serge Dassault, who is a senior member of the Gaullist party.
Belgian justice authorities had been trying since then to persuade their French counterparts to cooperate in the investigations.

The warrant was suddenly withdrawn last Friday, and news leaked out that investigators had managed to lay hands on some of the documents they wanted. But Belgium said the French authorities still refused to release 11 key documents.
Belgian Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck said this week he had written to and spoken to Guigou on the issue, but to little effect.

Willy Claes, a Belgian economics minister in the 1980s, was forced to resign as NATO secretary-general in 1995 over bribes alleged to have been paid to his Socialist Party by Dassault and Italian helicopter maker Agusta Spa.
